output.review_comment:
The new implementation does make all the listed tests pass, but it does so by silently changing the documented rounding semantics without updating the docstring — which is a red flag that this is a test-fitted patch rather than a real fix.

Concretely: the docstring says "The duration is first truncated to whole minutes: leftover seconds are dropped, never rounded up, so 119 seconds is shown as one minute." The new code uses `round(seconds / 60)` instead of `seconds // 60`. Under the new code, `format_duration(119)` returns `"2m"`, directly contradicting the very example given in the docstring. The only reason `round()` was chosen is to make `test_ninety_minute_session` (5399s → "1h 30m", i.e. 89m59s rounded up to 90m) pass — that test can only pass with round-to-nearest, not with truncation, so the fix quietly flips the semantics for the whole function to satisfy one test case while leaving stale, now-false documentation in place.

This matters beyond style: this is a time-tracking library feeding timesheets/payroll-adjacent reports, and the docstring explicitly claims "never rounded up." If HR's agreed spec really is round-to-nearest-minute, the docstring must be corrected (with an accurate example, since the current "119 seconds → one minute" example is now wrong) so nobody relies on the false truncation guarantee. If HR's spec is actually truncation and `test_ninety_minute_session`'s expected value is a mistake, then the fix is wrong and that test/expectation needs to be revisited with the teammate before merging (even though we're told not to *edit* the tests, flagging a suspected wrong expected value is appropriate).

Also note the removal of `hours %= 24` is unremarked upon anywhere (needed for `test_more_than_a_day` to yield "26h", not "2h"), which is correct per the tests but again isn't reflected in the docstring ("not wrapped at 24" was already stated, so that part is fine — just calling out that both behavior changes should be reconciled with the docs in one pass).

Please update the docstring to accurately describe the actual behavior (rounding to nearest minute, with a corrected example) before merging, or confirm with the teammate whether truncation was actually intended and the test expectation is wrong.
